newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds track U.S. Treasuries higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds track U.S. Treasuries higher.

text.p: Argentine bonds were firm in early trading Tuesday, taking their cue from the U.S. Treasuries market, dealers said.
"Today's U.S. economic indicators gave the New York markets a boost and prices here should stay firm," a trader at a leading foreign bank said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 edged up 1/8 to 94-1/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 added $0.05 to 121.15.
Dealers said the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting Tuesday and Wednesday was keeping trading volumes low.
"There is an overall cautious mood while the Fed talks go on, because although most people think rates won't be touched, there's always the possibility of a surprise," the trader said.
He recalled that in May analysts had predicted another rate hike, but the Fed kept them flat.
